letter:
I am appealing this Parking Charge Notice as the registered keeper of the vehicle LT12EST. The driver will not be identified.

The Notice to Keeper for PCN FRONTEND_LIVE_TEST_CPPLUS, relating to an event at LIVE_TEST Retail Park on 1 June 2026, was issued by post in England and Wales under the postal route of Schedule 4 to the Protection of Freedoms Act 2012. I note that the parking event is recorded as having taken place on 1 June 2026, while the Notice to Keeper was not issued until 20 June 2026. On the postal route, the statutory deadline for a Notice to Keeper to be delivered in these circumstances was 15 June 2026, with deemed delivery of this notice calculated as 23 June 2026. Accordingly, the Notice to Keeper was delivered 8 days outside the applicable statutory period for the relevant postal-notice route, so LIVE_TEST Parking Ltd has failed to satisfy a condition required to transfer liability to the registered keeper under Schedule 4. LIVE_TEST Parking Ltd has not established the identity of the driver, and because the applicable Schedule 4 timing requirements have not been satisfied, liability for this charge cannot be transferred to the registered keeper under Schedule 4.

For the reasons above, Schedule 4 keeper liability is not established; as the driver has not been identified there is no lawful basis to pursue this Parking Charge against the registered keeper on that footing. I invite LIVE_TEST Parking Ltd to cancel the Parking Charge Notice accordingly.

The operator has not established the identity of the driver. As the applicable Schedule 4 requirements have also not been satisfied, liability cannot be transferred to the registered keeper under Schedule 4. For the verified reasons set out above, the operator has not established keeper liability under Schedule 4 of the Protection of Freedoms Act 2012. The charge should therefore be cancelled as against the registered keeper. If the operator is not prepared to cancel the charge, it is requested to provide a clear response addressing the specific grounds and evidence raised.
